taglines: It is Saturday morning in summer and the light came in at 5:47am whether you wanted it to or not. The birds had opinions. The birds are still having opinions. You negotiated with a pillow for ninety minutes and the pillow won nothing and you won nothing and it is now 9am and here we are.

You have a 'system.' The system is three apps, a paper notebook, a voice memo you will never transcribe, and a deeply held belief that the next productivity tool will be the one that fixes everything. The system does not work. The system is the bit.

Summer solstice is tomorrow and the sun is going to peak and then start its long retreat and you did not accomplish the thing you said you would accomplish before the days started getting shorter and somehow the year is already half over and you have been 'in a season of building' since February.

Someone is at a farmer's market right now buying $14 jam and feeling morally superior to the grocery store and they are correct and you know it and you resent it and you should probably just go to the farmer's market.

The weekend stretches out ahead of you like an open road in a movie about freedom but you are going to spend the first two hours of it making a list of things to do on the weekend instead of doing the things and this is called planning and planning is productive so technically you are already winning.

Your phone has been on its charger for four hours and it is at 43% because you are running twelve things in the background including an argument you had three years ago that you have finally figured out how to win.

AI is everywhere now. In your search results, in your emails, in the customer service chat, in the code your coworker 'wrote,' in the article your favorite newsletter 'wrote,' in this. You spotted it though. You have good instincts. You are very perceptive. Anyway.

June 20th. Technically still the beginning of summer by the calendar even though emotionally it is already the part where summer is almost over and you have done none of the summer things. The summer things were always aspirational. You bought sunscreen. That counts.
